title: Navigating Alignment for Non-identical Client Class Sets: A Label Name-Anchored Federated Learning Framework

problem.claim: Federated classification with non-identical client class sets must learn a global model for the union of different or non-overlapping local class sets.

gap.claim: Existing methods assume a shared universal class set, while differing local latent spaces make server-side aggregation difficult.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes FedAlign, a framework for aligning client latent spaces from label and data perspectives.
FedAlign uses natural-language class names to anchor class representations and guide data-encoder learning across clients.
FedAlign uses global class representations and data points near or far from locally-unaware class anchors to align data encoders during local training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe FedAlign as a novel framework for this setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theoretical analysis and experiments on four real-world datasets confirm that FedAlign outperforms various state-of-the-art non-IID federated classification methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing federated classification methods generally assume a shared universal class set.
The paper addresses clients with different or non-overlapping class sets that require a global model covering their union.
Different client class sets can produce independent latent spaces that are difficult to aggregate.
FedAlign aligns latent spaces using label-name anchors and data-side alignment around global class representations.
The authors report theoretical and multi-dataset empirical support for improved performance over state-of-the-art non-IID methods.

source_observation.claim: Natural-language class names are used as a common ground for anchoring class representations across clients.

interpretation.claim: Semantic information associated with labels can help coordinate otherwise heterogeneous client representation spaces.

application.claim: In federated settings with mismatched label spaces, consider using shared label semantics to guide representation alignment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when class names are sufficiently consistent or informative for this alignment strategy.

source_observation.claim: Global class representations and local data points are used to align data encoders for locally-unaware classes.

interpretation.claim: Alignment can combine global semantic anchors with local examples rather than relying only on shared labels.

application.claim: For clients missing some classes, use relationships between local data and global class anchors as an auxiliary alignment signal.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the thresholds or conditions for data points to be considered close or far enough from anchors.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four datasets or their task domains.
It does not provide quantitative performance results, experimental settings, or baseline details.
It does not describe the theoretical assumptions or guarantees.
